subject: After-hours stability bulletin and customer briefing
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Green <samantha.green@cobalthealth.com>, Tom Reed <tom.reed@cobalthealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-01T00:12:00-07:00
Subject: After-hours stability bulletin: transient latency spike and mitigation plan

Samantha / Tom,

Quick note from the on-call team: between 23:45 and 00:05 PT we observed a short-lived latency surge affecting inference requests for your production model (request p99 increased to ~3.8s). The issue correlated with an autoscaling delay in a regional Dedicated pool in us-west-2 while a large batch rollout was in progress.

What we have done so far:
- Scoped impact: ~7% of requests saw degraded tails, no increased error rate.
- Applied targeted routing to warm replicas in another Dedicated pool to absorb traffic (00:00 PT).
- Rolled back the in-progress rollout and rebalanced the pool (00:18 PT).

Immediate commitments:
- We will keep the temporary routing in place for the next 4 hours and monitor p95/p99.
- Sharing the incident timeline and log snippets (attached).
- Follow-up executive summary to your leadership at 03:00 PT with RCA next steps.

Apologies for the disruption — we know this impacts your SLAs. I will remain on this thread and update you as we confirm stabilization.

— Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Senior Customer Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference
(direct) +1-415-555-0142
From: Samantha Green <samantha.green@cobalthealth.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Reed <tom.reed@cobalthealth.com>, CobaltHealth Oncall <oncall@cobalthealth.com>
Date: 2027-09-01T00:29:00-07:00
Subject: Re: After-hours stability bulletin: transient latency spike and mitigation plan

Thanks Dylan — appreciate the quick action. We saw some elevated user timeouts in a small subset of our traffic (primarily reports generation). No critical data loss, but this affected a handful of premium customers.

Can you confirm whether any requests were routed to a model variant with lower quantization? We need to ensure inference outputs remain within our expected tolerance for downstream scoring.

Samantha
Samantha Green
Head of Platform Operations, CobaltHealth
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-01T00:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: After-hours stability bulletin: transient latency spike and mitigation plan

Dylan — quick internal note: no model variant changes were performed. Routing switched to identical model version on a different pool (same quantization/profile). I pulled inference metadata: model_version=redwood-open-xxl-v2, quant=8bit, routing_policy=region-fallback.

Next steps for customer comms:
- Confirm no model variant mismatch (we did).
- Provide timeline and logs (attached).
- Offer a postmortem with action items within 72 hours and a small service credit proposal.

I can draft the executive note to leadership; Dylan can send to the customer.

— Marcus
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Green <samantha.green@cobalthealth.com>, Tom Reed <tom.reed@cobalthealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-01T01:02:00-07:00
Subject: Executive update: stabilization confirmed and next steps

Samantha / Tom — brief update:

Current status: stabilized. p95/p99 are back within normal baselines for the last 30 minutes. No route used a different quantization profile; traffic was shifted between identical model serving pools.

What caused it: an autoscaling hysteresis combined with an overlapping deployment in the us-west-2 Dedicated pool created a temporary capacity dip. We prevented errors by routing to healthy pools but the routing decision introduced tail latency for a minority of requests.

What we will deliver in the postmortem (ETA 72 hours):
- Root cause analysis with timeline and contributing factors.
- Action items: improved rollout gating, autoscaler tuning, and pre-warm thresholds.
- Compensatory proposal: one-time service credit equivalent to 3 days of usage for affected endpoints (formal offer to follow).

We understand the business impact and will provide a documented plan to reduce recurrence risk. Let me know if you want a short bridge call with our head of Ops (Laura) and your leadership before the full postmortem.

— Dylan
From: Tom Reed <tom.reed@cobalthealth.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Samantha Green <samantha.green@cobalthealth.com>
Cc: CobaltHealth Oncall <oncall@cobalthealth.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-01T03:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Executive update: stabilization confirmed and next steps

Appreciate the rapid response and clear commitments. A bridge call would be useful — can Laura join at 09:00 PT? Samantha and I will be available. Please send a calendar invite and include the postmortem doc when ready.

Tom
Tom Reed
VP Engineering, CobaltHealth
